A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CombatVLA study, including eight main-text pages, two reference pages and five supplementary pages. The text, equations, figures and tables are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, game-combat experiments, latency measurements and ablations in Section 5, plus supplementary token-length measurements and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the CUBench evaluation in Table 2, latency measurements in Table 3, game-combat results in Figure 5 and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The 3B model, AoT construction, three-stage progressive training, adaptive action-weighted losses and truncated inference procedure are unchanged in Section 4 and the supplementary details.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Black Myth: Wukong and Sekiro tasks, CUBench, MME, VideoMME and OCRBench. Training-task coverage and the 13 practical combat tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same VLM comparators. Figure 5 retains Cradle, the same VARP variants and human players; Figure 10 also retains the same reasoning-case comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain the 95%/5% training-validation split, training on tasks 9–10, identical zero-shot task assignments, training schedules and evaluation metrics. Game pausing and the modified character attributes for tasks 9–10 are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The progressive-learning and loss ablations in Tables 4–5, qualitative cases in Figures 6 and 9–10, and supplementary token-length analysis in Table 7 are identical.

E5.justification: Both specify 10 trials per task and report the same success-rate and average-latency summaries. Neither provides new seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. Examples include the 63.61 CUBench average in Table 2, 1.85-second latency in Table 3 and 116.57 versus 43.10 average token lengths in supplementary Table 7.

T1.justification: The frame-action alignment rule, priority-aware matching function and loss definitions in Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged, as are the supplementary action priorities and weights. No proofs or formal results are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning combat understanding, approximately 50-fold acceleration, generalization and higher task success than human players.

C2.justification: Interpretations of progressive learning, truncation, adaptive losses and generalization are identical. Supplementary Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning simplified tasks, coverage of only two games and remaining model-capability shortcomings.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, hardware, annotation procedures, tracker implementation and frame-processing details are unchanged. Both retain the same project link and prospective resource-release statement in supplementary Section 15.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 40 references are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes cited work or revises its relationship to earlier approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 12 March 2025 to v2 dated 9 January 2026. The title, authors, body text, headings and section order remain unchanged, including the supplement.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–7 retain the same content, captions, structure and placement. Visual inspection and comparison of embedded images and vector graphics establish no figure, table or substantive layout revision.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations and supplementary documentation of v1. The administrative version/date update does not meaningfully change clarity, evidential support or reproducibility.
